name: Pin the statement before solving
cue: Any problem. Especially OCR text, OEIS offsets, informal wording ("distinct", "surrounded", "abuts").

name: Explicit counterexample
cue: "Every n ...", "the only solutions are ...", "X is always prime/composite", "no n with ...".

name: Scan a complete table
cue: Universal or uniqueness claims about pseudoprimes, Carmichael numbers or sequence terms: "every Carmichael number ...", "the only ... are", "are there others besides ...".

name: Covering congruences
cue: "A·b^n + C is prime for some n", "for every x there is n with F(x, n) prime", families k·2^n ± 1, p + 2^n.

name: Congruence reduction to a constant
cue: "Infinitely many Carmichael numbers / pseudoprimes of the form p·g(p)".

name: Modular obstruction
cue: "X = Y has no solutions beyond ...", "every member of a family is a sum of ...".

name: Incremental SAT threshold
cue: "Least N such that every colouring / arrangement of [1, N] ...", existence of a small combinatorial object.

name: Finite verification of identities
cue: OEIS "Conjecture: a(n) = formula", "g.f. is ...", "satisfies the recurrence ...".

name: Parametric families plus a finite check
cue: "Every n ≥ N0 has a representation / two representations ...".

name: Density / union bound
cue: "Infinitely many n such that n − f(k) avoids P for all k", "every n is a sum of two numbers of type T".

name: Exact evaluation of real-valued statements
cue: Floors of roots, comparisons like n! vs m^m, "nearest x".

name: Units, Pell equations, continued fractions
cue: Sequences of n with a quadratic form value square ± constant; recurrences with palindromic coefficients; a(k+1) = a(k)^2 − 2.

name: Apply a classical theorem
cue: Coman-type "infinitely many pseudoprimes of form ..." claims and similar, where a classical construction already gives the family.

name: Direct elementary argument
cue: Anything settled by a short algebraic, combinatorial or number-theoretic argument not covered by another method.

name: Restatement, triviality, misstatement
cue: The item restates another one, is trivially true or false, or is misstated (OCR, wrong index).

name: Lean certificates in core Lean
cue: Any result whose evidence is a finite object or a finite computation, plus "for every n" claims reducible to finitely many facts and a periodicity lemma.

name: Layer LP with interval constraints
cue: Upper bounds for codes in hypercube-like graphs invariant under coordinate permutations, conflicts between nearby weights (Z-channel codes).

name: Asymptotics from polynomial recurrences
cue: OEIS "asymptotically", "a(n+1)/a(n) tends to", "mean of statistic ~ c n", "limit distribution is Poisson" for sequences with hypergeometric terms or P-recursive counts.

name: Creative telescoping certificate
cue: OEIS "Conjecture: (n+1)*a(n) - ... = 0" (P-recursive recurrence) for a(n) given as a finite sum of binomial or hypergeometric terms.

name: Local bounds for multiplicative counts
cue: OEIS "values of n with f(n) = n/k + 1" (or similar target) for a multiplicative counting function f such as the number of squares mod n; conjectures that such n are k*prime.

name: Generating-function coefficient extraction
cue: OEIS conjectures that a binomial sum, a binomial or Motzkin transform, or a difference of two sequences equals another sequence, where the generating functions are rational or algebraic.

name: Identify Nat.nth of a Diophantine set
cue: A sequence defined as "numbers m such that a quadratic form is a square" (or similar Diophantine set) has to be matched with an explicit recurrence or closed form.

name: Invariant for greedy sequences
cue: Sequences defined greedily ("smallest unused m such that ...") with a conjectured rule for passing from a(n) to a(n+1).

name: Finite witness for a continuous or asymptotic conjecture
cue: A conjecture about all sets, tilings, hypergraphs, Boolean functions or norms, where a counterexample would be one finite (or finitely described) object: "every hypergraph has tau <= ...", "every tile tiles periodically", "every set can be covered by d+1 smaller pieces".

name: Finite seed plus composition or tensor-power amplification
cue: A separation or ratio that must grow without bound ("bs(f) > s(f)^2 infinitely often", "variance exceeds degree by any factor", "O(n log n) can be beaten") where composing or tensoring objects multiplies the relevant measures.

name: Finite-field and finite-geometry constructions
cue: Extremal or Ramsey-type questions where random constructions are too weak or the extremal object should be highly symmetric: covering numbers of intersecting hypergraphs, graph homomorphism densities, colourings avoiding progressions, separated sets.

name: Minimal counterexample with strict local inequalities
cue: "Every graph/digraph/group with property P has Q", with no obvious induction; small cases verified by computer.

name: Analytic reduction to a compact region plus rigorous computation
cue: A sharp inequality or threshold depending on a few real parameters, where theory handles the asymptotic or generic range and a bounded leftover range remains.

name: LP / SDP / SOS dual certificates
cue: Optimal packings, energies, design or code nonexistence, sharp functional inequalities where an extremal configuration is conjectured.

name: Relax then round by discrepancy
cue: Find signs (or 0/1 values) for a sequence so that a family of linear functionals stays small: flat Littlewood polynomials, merit factor, Steinitz/prefix sums, balancing.

name: Limits from approximate superadditivity at dyadic sizes
cue: "lim a(n)/n exists", "the threshold converges", growth constants of combinatorial sequences when exact superadditivity fails by a small error.

name: Random construction with alteration and union bounds
cue: Existence of sets, colourings or graphs with many local constraints (hitting sets, avoiding configurations, Hadwiger-small graphs).

name: Selberg sieve for polynomial values in Lean
cue: Upper bounds for primes in pairs or tuples of linear forms (p and p + h prime, Goldbach-type m and 2n - m), Brun-type convergence, prime-gap growth claims.

name: Ordered prime gap bound for exact multiplicative targets
cue: Exact equations f(n) = n r (or phi(n) | n - 1, sigma(n) = 2n) with f multiplicative and local factors tending to 1: bound n for a fixed number of prime factors.

name: Cofactor exponent for Wieferich-type congruences
cue: Congruences a^(c-1) = 1 mod c^2 (or mod c^k) over composite c: Wieferich pseudoprimes, Fermat-quotient questions.

name: Macaulay-matrix ideal membership certificate
cue: Fixed-degree polynomial elimination: show a polynomial system forces some coefficients to vanish (Casas-Alvero in fixed degree, geometric configurations with polynomial constraints).

name: Flat orthogonal basis (Fourier, Hartley, Hadamard)
cue: A regular simplex, cross-polytope or orthonormal frame must fit in a small box or have small coordinates (simplices in cubes, packings of congruent copies, delocalised frames).

name: Reflective polynomial identity checker (kernel-evaluated certificates)
cue: A Lean proof needs large explicit polynomial identities (ideal-membership or elimination certificates with long or big-integer cofactors) that linear_combination / ring cannot normalise within the memory or time limit.
